english: Let $A(6,-2,6)$, $B(-4,-2,1)$, $C(-4,3,-3)$ and $D(-3,-4,5)$ be four points in space. Let $P$ be the point on the line $AB$ which is equidistant from $C$ and $D$. If $\overrightarrow{AP}=\lambda\,\overrightarrow{PB}$, then the value of $\lambda$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A(6,-2,6)$, $B(-4,-2,1)$, $C(-4,3,-3)$ तथा $D(-3,-4,5)$ आकाश में चार बिन्दु हैं। माना कि $P$ रेखा $AB$ पर वह बिन्दु है जो $C$ तथा $D$ से समदूरस्थ है। यदि $\overrightarrow{AP}=\lambda\,\overrightarrow{PB}$ है, तो $\lambda$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Every point of the line $AB$ is $P=A+t(B-A)$ with $B-A=(-10,0,-5)$, so $P=(6-10t,\,-2,\,6-5t)$.
$PC^2=PD^2$: the quadratic terms cancel and $206-290t=86-190t$, so $t=\dfrac{120}{100}=\dfrac65$. Hence $P=(-6,-2,0)$, a unique point.

$\overrightarrow{AP}=\lambda\overrightarrow{PB}$ means $P=\dfrac{A+\lambda B}{1+\lambda}$ (section formula), that is $P=A+\dfrac{\lambda}{1+\lambda}(B-A)$, so $\dfrac{\lambda}{1+\lambda}=\dfrac65$, giving $5\lambda=6+6\lambda$ and $\lambda=-6$.

Check: $\overrightarrow{AP}=(-12,0,-6)$ and $\overrightarrow{PB}=(2,0,1)$, so $\overrightarrow{AP}=-6\,\overrightarrow{PB}$; $P$ divides $AB$ externally, beyond $B$. Also $PC^2=4+25+9=38=9+4+25=PD^2$.
originality_note: New: the line AB is cut by the condition PC = PD; the quadratic terms of the two distance formulas cancel to give the parameter, which the section formula turns into a signed ratio that comes out external (way 5). Closest known: ratio in which a coordinate plane divides a segment. Different because: the dividing set is given only as an equidistance condition, and the answer is the signed ratio of an external division.
blueprint_concepts: Coordinates in space; distance and section formulae

concept_use.Coordinates in space; distance and secti: The distance formula writes PC^2 = PD^2 for a general point of AB, and the section formula P = (A + lambda B)/(1 + lambda) converts the parameter t = 6/5 into lambda = -6.

stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, vector and plane is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/numpy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Wrote the ratio as the vector relation AP = lambda PB so the sign convention is unambiguous; P exists and is unique because the equation in t is linear with non-zero coefficient. Changed: No change.
key_step: Equating squared distances from a general point of AB, where the t^2 terms cancel, then converting t to the signed section ratio.
justification: Routine chain of distance formula, a linear equation and the section formula; the only trap is the sign of an external division. Above the direct section checks of 2023-P2-Q4 (L1) because of the chain and the numerical format.
